citation.authors: Dale HF, Jensen C, Hausken T, Lied E, Hatlebakk JG, Brønstad I, Lihaug Hoff DA, Lied GA
citation.title: Effect of a cod protein hydrolysate on postprandial glucose metabolism in healthy subjects: a double-blind cross-over trial

population.description: Forty-one healthy, active men (15) and women (26) aged 40-64 (Results: 'range 40-64 years'; Table 3 age 51.0 (sd 6.0); BMI 25.2 (sd 3.0), Table 3; no BMI range printed). Healthy as the paper calls them ('healthy and active individuals'), screened by a physician's examination and baseline biochemistry, with pharmacologically treated diabetes and elevated blood pressure excluded (Methods, Participants). Crossover: the same 41 people had both study days.

protocols.name: casein_breakfast
protocols.description: Control (casein drink) study day, the only meal arm entered: drink and breakfast served at arm minute 0 (the paper gives arrival 08.00 to 09.00; 08:00 assumed); meal = 77 g carbohydrate (printed: 'including the drink, the breakfast provided in total 500 kcal and 77 g carbohydrate'; 41 g breakfast + 35.9 g drink = 76.9), 15 g fat (breakfast; the drink powder is 4 % protein and 96 % maltodextrin, so no fat), 14.1 g protein (derived: 12.5 g breakfast + 1.6 g in the drink, 'on average 1.6 g'). Energy check: 355 kcal breakfast + 145 kcal drink = 500 kcal. Sampling clock: Methods say 'The first post-meal sample (0 min sample) was taken 15 min after the breakfast was served', so table time T is arm minute 15 + T (minutes 15 to 195). The Fig. 3 legend ('0 min shows values measured right after the intake of breakfast and test material') and the Results ('peak ... 20 min after the meal', which is the table's 20 min row) are less exact and not in conflict if eating took about 15 min; the paper does not say how long the meal took, so Methods' 15 min is kept and a shift of the whole table clock by up to 15 min cannot be excluded. Subjects ate a standardised evening meal before 20.30 (contents not printed, not entered) and fasted until the morning; prefast_hours 11.5 = 20.30 to 08.00 (the paper's 'before 20.30' and arrival from 08.00 make this a lower bound, taken as the value).

meals.food: semi-coarse bread, margarine, strawberry jam, white cheese, casein drink

protocols.name: casein_day_fasted_arrival
protocols.description: Baseline sample of the control (casein) study day: drawn on arrival, after the fast and before the drink and breakfast were served ('After blood samples, they were served a drink'). The paper prints no time between the sample and the serving, so a 30 min fasted run-in stands for the single sample (README convention), the value read at minutes 29 to 30. No meal. Arrival 08.00 to 09.00 (08:00 assumed); prefast_hours 11.5 as for the meal arm (evening meal before 20.30, then fasting).
